column1: # Every title rule, one row each: the prefixes, suffixes, banners and spellings the title pipeline takes off or unifies
# (services.titlerules.TitleRuleTable reads it; TitleRuleSet folds it). Data, not code: a new banner is a new row.
# Inventory, firing counts and the merges behind it: docs/investigations/2026-10-22-rule-consolidation.md.
# id<TAB>kind<TAB>cinema<TAB>countries<TAB>flags<TAB>effect<TAB>season<TAB>pattern<TAB>replacement<TAB>note<TAB>examples
#   kind:      the mechanism that applies the row —
#                banner  a programme banner off the front of the LOOKUP query; the display finds it too, to case the
#                        banner and the film apart ("Klub Konesera: Ojczyzna" searches as "Ojczyzna")
#                query   a strip or rewrite of the LOOKUP query only: the screening keeps its own row and merge key
#                key     a fold of the MERGE KEY (and, when it rewrites, the display spelling): spellings of one film
#                        collapse into one row — a rewrite writing words names its countries (TitleRule.countryScopeValid)
#                name    a key rewrite to a broadcaster's proper name, the same words in every country
#                venue   one venue's cleanup at ingest (cinema = its TitleRuleKey; a chain's venues share one)
#   countries: blank = every country; else the codes (pl, uk, de, us, es) whose processes load the row
#   flags:     all = replace every match (default: the first); seed = the frozen pre-rules baseline (TitleRules,
#              pinned by ProdTitlesNormalizationSpec against the legacy code)
#   effect:    what the row takes off — banner, audience, event, edition, format, festival, retrospective, relay
#              (a relay house's banner; RelayStage owns those houses), rename, venue, junk. Descriptive only, but
#              relay: identity reads a relay row's banner as a fact (RelayBanner, RelayRecords).
#   season:    the months its billing comes back in (jun-sep, dec-feb, oct…). Descriptive only: a seasonal row stays in
#              force all year, so next summer's banner is stripped the day it is billed.
#   pattern:   a Java regex; {{NAME}} placeholders expand from TitleRulePlaceholders first.
#   replacement: Regex replacement ("" = strip; $1 = a group).
#   examples:  REQUIRED, a JSON list of [billing, reading] pairs: what the row's tier makes of the billing under the
#              rules of the first country holding it — the lookup query (banner, query), the merge-key fold (key), the
#              proper name (name), the venue's cleanup (venue). TitleRuleExamplesSpec holds every row to its examples;
#              TitleRuleMutationSpec removes each row and asks that one of them change (the row is load-bearing), save
#              the rows it lists as covered by another row or the billing parse. A row without one fails to load.
# ORDER IS MEANING: each tier (banner+query, key+name) and each venue folds its rows top to bottom, each on the last
# one's output. A row placed above another runs first.
# ═══ The lookup tier: banner + query rows (TitleRuleSet.structural, the external search's query) ═══════════════════
# NOT in the merge key: a decoration or programme edition keys by its own form, so the screening keeps its own row
# ("Kino bez barier: …" stays apart from the film) while its query finds the film's ratings and poster. The seed's
# programme, accessibility and event strips fold first, then the "+ <event>" strip, the Cykl banner, the slash and
# decoration suffixes; every later row after them. A GlobalStructural decoration MERGE ("<film> /Kino Cafe" onto the
# film) does not belong here — it does not change the merge key, so the stale and the base row collide on hydration —
# it is a venue row. A generic "<anything>: <film>" banner never does either: it amputates real titles ("Rocky IV:
# Ostateczna walka"); each banner here is anchored to its own words.
search-programme-prefix

column1: # Polish summer/holiday and family cycles. Every one of these was found on a row
# that reached TMDB with the banner still attached and therefore matched nothing —
# "Big Festivalowski: …" alone accounted for 22 unresolved rows in the real corpus.
# Each is anchored to a literal banner rather than a generic "<anything>: <film>",
# because a generic colon rule amputates real titles ("Rocky IV: Ostateczna walka").
# Twenty-first wave (2026-08-23), from the convergence leg's TMDB-no-match list:
# the same numbered-festival shape as the two named rules above, but generic in the
# festival's NAME rather than needing one rule per festival. Anchored three ways so
# it stays a banner rule and not a blind "strip anything before a colon": a leading
# edition ORDINAL, the literal word Festiwal/Festival, and a terminating colon, with
# `{{NSEP}}` guarding the name so the match stops at the first hard separator.
# That guard is what keeps a NESTED strand conservative: '12. Przeźrocza Festiwal
# Filmowy: Klasyka Gatunku: "Człowiek z żelaza"' loses only the festival banner and
# keeps 'Klasyka Gatunku: …', because stripping a second unnamed 'Word: ' prefix is
# exactly the dangerous shape the programme-prefix audit warns about.
# Query-only, like every rule here: the festival screening keeps its own display row
# and merge key (Kino Orzeł lists these as festival rows and they must stay that
# way), and only the external lookup sees the bare film. Verified on TMDB:
# '"Zmruż oczy"' → 2003, '"Żywot Mateusza"' → 1968, '"Niespodziewane"' → 2026 —
# the wrapping quotes are harmless to the search and are deliberately kept (see the
# '"Whiplash"' negative control).
# Twenty-third wave (2026-08-29), from the Poland convergence leg's IDENTIFICATION
# gap rather than from a rating-less list. That leg scores the replay's tmdbId share
# against production's on the same repertoire, and it had drifted 5.3% under a 5%
# band. Most of the gap is production's HISTORY — a row that won its id under an
# earlier, cleaner spelling, which a cold single-pass replay cannot reproduce — but
# these three banners are ordinary missing rules, each on a shape a sibling rule
# just fails to reach. Every base film verified on TMDB.
#  - 'Avant Art. Festival 2026: <film>'. The generic numbered-festival rule
#    (xtra-pp-numbered-festival) wants the edition ORDINAL first ('12. … Festiwal
#    …:'); this festival puts its YEAR after the name and abbreviates with a full
#    stop, so neither that rule nor the named ones reach it. Spelled both
#    'Festival' and 'Festiwal' across the four cinemas that carry it.
# Eighth-wave (2026-06-20) audit of the rating-less corpus (1165-title prod
# snapshot replayed through the rule engine): festival / audience / club colon
# banners that prefix the film (own display row, query stripped to the bare film).
# · xtra-pp-big-festivalowski: Big Festivalowski festival cycle

column1: xtra-pipe-cycle-banner
column10: '<film> | <cycle/festival banner>' generic PIPE-suffix strip, keyword-guarded so it only fires when the segment right after the pipe is a recognised cycle word — never amputates a 'Banner | Film' shape where the film FOLLOWS the pipe (KINO SENIORA | Ojczyzna, LATO w LUNIE | Drzewo magii, FEDERICO FELLINI: ciao a tutti! | GŁOS Z KSIĘŻYCA stay intact). The keyword list is the whole rule: a 2026-09-05 audit found 56 PL films known ONLY by a pipe-suffixed strand, 32 of them (57%, against a ~26% corpus baseline) with no TMDB id because the strand went into the search query — 'Młode Horyzonty' alone accounted for 52. Widening the guard is how this rule grows; loosening it is how it eats a film. ONE MEASURED SIDE EFFECT, traced end to end 2026-09-05: a decorated row stops INHERITING the base film's release year. The Kinoteka listing of "90. urodziny Pavarottiego" has its own detail page, and that page states no year at all (only a 95-minute runtime); the 2026 it used to carry came from the BARE row, whose detail does state it. Stripping the strand keeps the two apart, so `MovieCache.venueSlotYear` finds no year on the venue's slot and the row is never promoted from a yearless key onto 2026. That is the rule working — a decorated edition is not the base film — and the row keeps the year its own source actually gives, which is none. It costs that card its year pill, against 52 films whose TMDB query this fixes and a fixture row ("Kolor purpury | Kinoteka jest Kobietą") that goes from a 2026 key with no synopsis to Spielberg's 1985 film. Worth knowing because it means a search-tier keyword CAN move a stored key year, by way of what the row is allowed to be merged with

# contains an already-RATED film title as a substring proves the surrounding
# text is strippable decoration (and the inner film is rated by construction).

# they never strip it: the broadcast stays its own card, apart from any film of the work's name (a ballet
# 'Manon' is not a film 'Manon'; see the fourteenth-wave note above). Ordered after the bracketed-year strip,
